member.name: T:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Utilities.ExportingSideBySideActivationContextScope
member.summary: A scope for access the exporting stuff like GAML or AnDI
member.remarks:
It is possible to access COM components (like the Formula One, GAML or AnDI) on Windows XP/Vista as so called "Side by Side assemblies" with the Activation Context API (see MSDN).
This allows to use multiple instances of a COM component in an "XCOPY" manner without globally registering it with regsvr32. This means that the COM dll can simply be copied to the executable path of an application without affecting any other applications.
This works by an "Application Manifest" for the executable that is started and a "Component Manifest" that exposes the COM component as a set of registration free interfaces, more specific: the application has an application manifest that references a component manifest for the side by side proxy of the SDK that points to the corresponding COM dll.
To avoid providing application manifests for each application (including test-harnesses) the application manifest that configures the activation context of the application when it is started by Windows is replaced by an application manifest that configures a "virtual" activation context that is created dynamically.
